scenario.thought: My sister keeps commenting on my weight at family dinners. Thanksgiving is next week and I'm thinking of just not going.

state.thought: My sister keeps commenting on my weight at family dinners. Thanksgiving is next week and I'm thinking of just not going.

steps: By Monday, text [Sister's name]: 'Can we talk before Thanksgiving? Your comments about my weight hurt, and I need them to stop.'

By Monday, ask [Companion]: 'Will you come to Thanksgiving and sit beside me at the table? Can we agree now, privately, on an arm touch if my sister comments? When I touch your arm, turn toward me and keep talking with me.' Seat whoever says yes beside me. If [Companion] hasn't said yes by Monday, ask [Backup person] the same day with the same words and seat them beside me.

By Monday, text Mom: 'I'm coming with [Companion or Backup person]. Can I take [task], like the rolls? A yes or no by Monday helps me plan.' If she hasn't answered by Tuesday, text: 'Can you confirm that I'm taking [task] for Thanksgiving?'

anger.why: Her comments cross a line, and skipping dinner just dodges it. Nobody has named that.

embarrassment.why: Missing Thanksgiving could strain the relationships we're trying to protect. Check with me first.

loneliness.why: A holiday alone, cut off from everyone at the table, sounds lonely.

guilt.why: Who absorbs the hurt if I vanish? Mom and the others would miss me.

fear.need: Mom names my task and confirms it by Monday.
fear.why: If I stop showing up, the family could drift and I'd lose ground.

messages.text: My sister keeps commenting on my weight at family dinners. Thanksgiving is next week and I'm thinking of just not going.
Here's the move: I skip Thanksgiving next week and her comments stop being my problem. Once everyone sees how simple that is, we can get on with the week.

Skipping dinner only takes me out of the room. Her comments stay in her mouth and show up at the next gathering, because nobody has told her the line exists. By Monday next week, I need you to have me text [Sister's name]: 'Your comments about my weight hurt me. Stop them, or I'll leave the table.' Until that message is sent, I stay at -1.
messages.why: Skipping dodges the line she crossed. Name the boundary first.

messages.text: Skipping Thanksgiving takes me out of the room, but it doesn't reach my need: the relationships still need protecting, and my absence could look like a rift that leaves Mom and the others guessing. What would work is a private text to [Sister's name] before Thanksgiving, so she hears the boundary before anyone is at the table: 'Can we talk before Thanksgiving? Your comments about my weight hurt, and I need them to stop.' Anger's wording can stay, but I want it sent privately, not at dinner.
messages.why: Nobody checked with me before the Thanksgiving skip or the text.

messages.text: Honestly, it's just family being family. Don't overthink it, and maybe just let it roll off your back over pie.

Society's 'let it roll off your back' skips what hurts me: my sister's comments get said where everyone can hear, and I'm the one who has to take the moment and then sit at the table. Following it means the same comments again, in front of Mom and the others, with no one having told her the line exists. Embarrassment's text keeps it private and before Thanksgiving, so the table never becomes the venue. I can live with that as the plan.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Skipping leaves you alone at the table, and Guilt and Fear both point at Mom and the others missing you and the family drifting, so I'm dropping it. I keep Embarrassment's private text to [Sister's name] as written and hold Anger's Monday deadline for it. Path A is built for Loneliness by bringing a companion so you're not alone at the table; Path B is built for Guilt and Fear by telling Mom ahead of time and leaving before pie.

Path A only meets me if [companion] actually says yes, and Path B leaves me alone at the table for the first hour. I need Path A's ask to [companion] answered with a yes by Monday next week, so I know who will sit beside me before Thanksgiving. If they can't come, I need the user to name one other person by Monday next week who will sit beside them at the table.
messages.why: A companion's maybe isn't company; I need a yes before Thanksgiving.

messages.text: Path B tells Mom I'm leaving early, but it doesn't keep my place in the family: a first-hour visit with an exit before pie can read as pulling back, and the drift I'm afraid of stays untouched. What would work is a text to [Mom] by Monday next week: 'Could you tell me if anyone needs me for Thanksgiving, like helping in the kitchen or setting the table?' That gives me a concrete role and keeps me visibly part of the day whichever path we take.
messages.why: Without a Monday yes or a named backup, Path A leaves others exposed.

messages.text: Give it some time and it'll sort itself out. Families usually settle down once everyone's gotten used to each other again.

Waiting for it to sort itself out leaves my need completely untouched: nothing about time delivers the line to my sister or makes her comments stop before Thanksgiving. Following it means the next remark lands at the table in front of Mom and the others, with her still not knowing the line exists. Time doesn't text anyone, so only Embarrassment's private message gets her to hear it before the day.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Path A wins because Anger, Loneliness, Guilt, and Embarrassment all need someone beside you at the table and the boundary delivered privately before the day. Mom and the others would miss me if I vanished, and that's the hurt I'm holding onto. Plan v3 answers it: the text to [Mom] tells her I'm coming and bringing [Companion], so she hears from me first that I'm showing up. I can live with this at 0, on the condition that the Mom text goes out by Monday next week and gets a Tuesday follow-up if she hasn't replied.
messages.why: Mom hearing it first and showing up answers who absorbs the hurt.
